originalTitle: Russia and North Korea finalising first road crossing amid concerns it serves as Ukraine war supply route
summary: New bridge makes it easier to dodge satellite surveillance, investigation argues, as Ukrainian president warns Russia is to receive 30,000 more North Korean soldiers
content: Russia and North Korea are close to completing a bridge that will form the first road link ever built between them, amid concerns the two increasingly close allies are creating infrastructure to boost military cooperation in the Ukraine war. The bridge spans the Tumen River, between Khasan in Russia’s far east and Tumangang in North Korea, a remote, thinly populated stretch of borderland where the river marks the final few miles of the frontier before it reaches the coast. The crossing is now largely complete. North Korea finished its side of the project, including customs and quarantine facilities, ahead of a planned opening on 19 June, but Russia has fallen behind on its own side of the border, and no new opening date has been confirmed. Russian and North Korean authorities have made no secret of the bridge project, saying it is intended to expand trade and tourism. North Korea’s state media news agency, KCNA, has similarly cast the bridge as a way to boost “travel of persons, tourism and circulation of commodities” between the two countries. However, a new investigation by Ukrainian human rights group Truth Hounds and shared with the Guardian suggests it is intended more to provide a discreet military logistics corridor than to boost trade. Nazar Myhun, who led the open-source research at Truth Hounds, said a key reason behind its conclusion was the fact that it is much easier to evade satellite monitoring – a surveillance method used by the west to understand Russian and North Korean activities – by using roads compared with a rail network. The new crossing over the Tumen River runs alongside the Friendship Bridge, which is the only rail link between the two countries. Russia and North Korea’s road network is far bigger than their rail network, he said, making it harder to watch in its entirety. Loading and unloading of trucks can also take place much more quickly than for railcars, which are exposed to satellite passes for a longer period of time. “The type of railcar visible in an image reveals a great deal about the cargo, and certain categories of goods are transported in open railcars, which allows them to be identified,” Myhun told the Guardian. “Trucks, by contrast, almost always look the same in satellite imagery.” Road cargo can also be loaded anywhere, as opposed to trains, which rely on a handful of fixed rail hubs, Myhun said. Russian officials have presented the project as a way to expand trade and tourism. Andrey Nikitin, Russia’s transport minister, said: “The opening of the new road bridge will increase mutual trade, optimise logistics, strengthen cultural ties, and transform border areas into dynamically developing economic hubs.” However, Truth Hounds argues that the bridge’s economic rationale is weak. The crossing is estimated to have cost more than $100m, versus bilateral trade that was reportedly worth just $34m in 2024. Tourism from Russia into North Korea remains tightly controlled and largely limited to escorted tours, with around 10,000 Russian visitors in 2025. Pyongyang, where most foreign tourists visit, lies over 500km from the crossing. Instead, the investigation concludes that the crossing is better understood as strategic infrastructure: a corridor for moving North Korean troops, construction brigades and military officials into Russia, and for Russian technology and resources to move in the opposite direction. Myhun said Truth Hounds monitors Russia-North Korea cooperation closely because it considers it “one of the key factors affecting Russia’s strength in this war” on Ukraine. The deepening relationship has also made the two-way exchange of weapons and technology between the two countries “easier and less transparent”, he said, which also poses a threat to North Korea’s neighbours. The Kremlin has been contacted about the claims made in the investigation but has yet to respond. A growing military alliance The bridge over the Tumen River is about 1km long and seven metres wide, with two lanes, part of a wider 4.7km crossing that includes approach roads. Satellite imagery also shows supporting infrastructure being built on the Russian side, including a helicopter landing pad. However, the rail line is hobbled by a mismatch in rail gauge between Russia and North Korea, meaning wheelsets must be changed to allow trains to travel further into either country’s network, a limitation the new road bridge does not share. Open-source researchers have previously relied on satellite imagery of the rail crossing to monitor suspected weapons transfers between the two countries. Construction of the bridge began after Vladimir Putin and Kim Jong-un signed a comprehensive strategic partnership pact in June 2024, cementing military ties that have since seen North Korea provide troops, artillery ammunition and ballistic missiles to support Russia’s war in Ukraine. It forms a small part of a much broader military relationship. More than 14,000 North Korean troops have fought alongside Russian forces in the Kursk region, after Ukraine staged a surprise counter-invasion in August 2024. Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy has now warned that Russia is preparing to receive a further 30,000 soldiers. Moscow and Pyongyang have expanded cooperation on weapons, military technology and reconstruction. In 2023, Reuters reported that satellite images showed an estimated 2,000 containers exported from the North Korean port of Rason to Russia, believed to have contained artillery shells and possibly short-range missiles. Kim has praised North Korean soldiers who fought and died for Russia and unveiled housing for the families of those killed. At least 2,000 North Korean servicemen are believed to have died fighting in Russia’s war, with two badly wounded soldiers taken prisoner.
chineseTitle: 俄罗斯和朝鲜敲定第一个公路过境点，担心它成为乌克兰战争补给线
chineseSummary: 调查称，新桥更容易躲避卫星监视，乌克兰总统警告俄罗斯将再接收 30,000 名朝鲜士兵
chineseContent: 俄罗斯和朝鲜即将建成一座桥梁，这将成为两国之间有史以来第一条公路连接，人们担心这两个日益亲密的盟友正在建设基础设施，以促进乌克兰战争中的军事合作。这座桥横跨图们江，位于俄罗斯远东地区的哈桑和朝鲜的图满江之间。图们江是一个偏远、人口稀少的边境地区，这条河标志着边境到达海岸之前的最后几英里。穿越现已基本完成。朝鲜在计划于 6 月 19 日开放之前完成了其一侧的项目，包括海关和检疫设施，但俄罗斯在边境一侧的进度却落后了，并且尚未确认新的开放日期。俄罗斯和朝鲜当局毫不掩饰这座桥梁项目，称其目的是扩大贸易和旅游业。朝鲜官方媒体朝中社也同样将这座桥视为促进两国之间“人员流动、旅游和商品流通”的一种方式。然而，乌克兰人权组织“真相猎犬”与《卫报》分享的一项新调查表明，其目的更多是提供一条谨慎的军事后勤走廊，而不是促进贸易。 Truth Hounds 开源研究的负责人 Nazar Myhun 表示，其结论背后的一个关键原因是，与铁路网络相比，使用公路更容易逃避卫星监控（西方国家用来了解俄罗斯和朝鲜活动的监视方法）。新的图们江过境点沿着友谊大桥延伸，友谊大桥是连接两国的唯一铁路线。他说，俄罗斯和朝鲜的公路网远大于铁路网，这使得它们
